StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only. ShouldScaleInMultiplayer / GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer feed PowerCmd.Apply's MultiplayerScalingModel leg (PowerCmd.cs:128-131), waived as step 14 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json.

GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only. ShouldScaleInMultiplayer / GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer feed PowerCmd.Apply's MultiplayerScalingModel leg (PowerCmd.cs:128-131), waived as step 14 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json.

AfterAttack.issue: C#'s hook is AfterAttack, which fires ONCE per AttackCommand after every hit has landed (SkittishPower.cs:56-69 searches command.Results for a DamageResult whose Receiver is the owner); the sim uses on_damage_received, which fires PER HIT. The once-per-turn gate makes the totals agree, but the TIMING does not: the sim grants the block after the first qualifying hit, so the second and later hits of a multi-hit Attack card are absorbed by block the game has not granted yet. Identical shape to power/curl_up's, whose C# also defers to the end of the card play, and reachable the same way -- the ported Phantasmal Gardener plus any multi-hit Attack. The sim does have the AfterAttack slot available: hooks.py:361-370 after_attack, used by VigorPower and GigantificationPower. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE SLOT HALF IS CLOSED: the reset is now `after_player_turn_end` (powers.py:1927), the sim's Hook.AfterTurnEnd slot (combat.py:809 / CombatManager.cs:1307). WHAT REMAINS is the side test: SkittishPower.cs:73 acts only when `side != base.Owner.Side`, while powers.py:1927-1929 resets on every player turn end regardless of the owner's side. For an enemy-owned Skittish -- the only ported case, the Phantasmal Gardener -- the two agree; a player-owned one would reset at the wrong side's end. Dormant, unchanged.

guards.rationale: powers.py:1810 `ValueProp.MOVE in props`. Identical -- and note this is the weaker Move test, NOT IsPoweredAttack, so an UNPOWERED Move (a status card damaging the player) does qualify on both sides. The sim gets the distinction right where power/thorns and power/curl_up drop their gates entirely.
powers.py:1809 `card is not None`. Identical: only card attacks trigger Skittish, not monster moves or powers.
powers.py:1811 `amount > 0`; the sim's amount is the post-block unblocked loss (cmds.py:122). C#'s `!= 0` and the sim's `> 0` agree because unblocked damage is never negative.
powers.py:1808 `not self._blocked_this_turn`, set at :1814 before the block gain exactly as C# sets its flag at :63 before its GainBlock.
powers.py:1816-1818 passes `props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED` explicitly. One of the eight powers that get this right.

powers.py:1812. C# reaches AfterAttack only through the attack pipeline and would gain block on a dying creature; the sim's guard is defensive and cannot produce a divergence, because block on a dead creature is discarded either way.
